exact_title: The comparative efficacy of SGLT-2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists on metabolic benefits in T2DM patients: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
substantive_page_range: Main article pages 1–8; disclosures/references pages 9–10; supplement pages 1–57

main_figures.topic: Class-level body-weight network and forest plot
Individual-drug body-weight network and forest plot
HbA1c, blood pressure, and lipid forest plots

supplement_appendices.content: Search strategy; PRISMA flow; database search tables
Study/participant characteristics and baseline transitivity information
Individual-drug body-weight network, SUCRA, and league table
Secondary-outcome class-level and individual HbA1c analyses
Small-trial exclusion sensitivity analyses (source numbering malformed)
Frequentist network meta-analysis sensitivity (source numbering malformed)

visual_strategy.structured_blocks: All main figures/table and all 12 materially relevant supplement appendices
omitted_with_reason: Individual 168-study rows and every convergence/funnel/node-splitting panel are summarized as their semantic appendix object rather than duplicated panel-by-panel; the original supplement remains the visual source of record.

batch_plan.scope: Included evidence base and bias/certainty results
Class and individual-drug weight results plus BMI subgroups

coverage_decision: Full main-text coverage plus all 12 supplement appendices because they materially affect methods, result interpretation, sensitivity, or appraisal. References were transcribed separately as a task queue and not atomized.
omissions: Bibliography entries were not treated as evidence atoms.
Individual underlying RCT results were not re-attributed to the review as primary evidence.

source_integrity_findings.issue: The reported GLP-1RA vs SGLT-2i point estimate (−1.11 kg) lies outside the stated 95% CrI (−6.73 to −4.60), so the interval cannot be mathematically valid as printed.
source_integrity_findings.handling: Preserved exactly as reported; not corrected.

source_integrity_findings.issue: Results reports 8 GLP-1 receptor agonists and 9 SGLT-2 inhibitors, while the strengths paragraph reports 7 GLP-1 receptor agonists and 8 SGLT-2 inhibitors.
source_integrity_findings.handling: Results count retained as the main study-characteristics statement; discrepancy flagged.

source_integrity_findings.issue: Discussion attributes weight MD −1.96 kg and LDL-c −0.24 mmol/L to GLP-1 receptor agonists; the main results report GLP-1RA weight MD −3.03 kg and LDL-c −0.14 mmol/L versus placebo, while −1.96 kg is the SGLT-2i weight estimate.
source_integrity_findings.handling: No silent correction; appraisal flags the contradiction.

source_integrity_findings.issue: The printed direction-of-effect note (MD<0 favors column; MD>0 favors row) appears inconsistent with the narrative interpretation of the GLP-1RA vs SGLT-2i BMI subgroup estimates.
source_integrity_findings.handling: Table values preserved; directional interpretation treated cautiously.

source_integrity_findings.issue: GLP-1RA triglyceride 95% CrI lower bound is −0.22 mmol/L in the abstract but approximately −0.21 mmol/L in Figure 4.
source_integrity_findings.handling: Figure 4 value used for the figure-derived atom; abstract discrepancy flagged.

source_integrity_findings.issue: Appendix/table numbering is internally inconsistent (e.g., Appendix 11 labeled “Appendix 1 1,” sensitivity table labeled S9.1, frequentist table labeled S10.1 despite another S10.1 in Appendix 10).
source_integrity_findings.handling: Coverage uses semantic appendix labels rather than trusting duplicate table numbers.

source_integrity_findings.issue: HbA1c sensitivity values are on a body-weight-like scale and do not match the primary HbA1c estimates, consistent with a likely transcription/copy-paste error.
source_integrity_findings.handling: These malformed values were not normalized into atoms.

source_integrity_findings.issue: Several entries contain malformed or internally impossible estimate/interval formatting.
source_integrity_findings.handling: Frequentist validation is retained only as the source’s qualitative sensitivity claim; malformed cells are not converted into quantitative atoms.
